summary:
Adding canonical sampling mutants changes the full rejection census even when focused preflight passes: focused mode exits before the full terminal guard. The maintained validator now names the actual mutant list once, checks uniqueness and observed rejection delta before focused exit, and derives its full rejection expectation from the retained 71 established base controls, that list, and five rejected calls per formal scenario. The current source declares 21 mutants, nine roots and nineteen formal scenarios: 92 base and 187 full rejected calls, with 289 external, 254 Quint and 71 verification logical calls in the full inventory. These are source-derived expected counts, not a newly observed whole qualification result.

A dependency-free pure preflight joins positive/mutant/replay lists, declared invocation roles and configured root/formal inventories before the canonical entry launches CLR tools. The current aggregate consumes its derived base census; typed receipt digest, logical/physical predicates and current synthetic fixture are checked against the same plan. Formal reuse, offline source binding and optimistic harness identities include the helper and its current source readers. Historical native fixture bytes retain their exact original 79-rejection predicate; they are not current receipts.

The old accepted measurement baseline remains immutable historical evidence. Changing canonical source, configuration or validator bytes requires a fresh complete measurement and separately reviewed baseline admission. Source and pure causal/predicate controls do not establish FSI compilation, exhaustive formal acceptance, native ABI closure, generator memory fit, publication or whole #4820/#4650 acceptance. The original failed CI and later aborted probe remain failures outside Atlas; no retry or new qualification is inferred.
title: Current canonical qualification accounting follows the declared source inventory
